questions.stem: A nurse is documenting an assessment of a client receiving treatment for a substance use disorder. Which chart entry best reflects objective, person-first, non-stigmatizing language?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"“Client with a substance use disorder reports two episodes of nonprescribed substance use this week and asks to review available treatment supports.”","B":"“Substance abuser relapsed twice this week but is finally asking for help, showing improved willingness to take responsibility for the problem.”","C":"“Client had two dirty episodes this week and should demonstrate better compliance before additional treatment resources are offered.”","D":"“Substance-use concerns were discussed, but specific use was omitted from the record to avoid documenting information that might stigmatize the client.”"}}
questions.rationale: Person-first, objective language describes the clinical condition and reported behavior without stigmatizing labels or moral judgment. Clinically relevant substance-use information should be documented accurately rather than omitted solely to avoid stigma.
questions.source_name: SAMHSA — Stigma and Language: The Power of Perceptions and Understanding
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA identifies negative attitudes, beliefs, and stigmatizing language as barriers to treatment and supports respectful, non-stigmatizing communication about substance use disorders.

qc.qc_note: Strict Wave-6 anti-cue rule: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; correct option is neither unique shortest nor unique longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility and wording cues.
